chapter: Eddie South, high school and the South Side scene
title: Joe Sutler, the highest-paid Chicago trumpeter nobody mentions
summary: Hinton praises Joe Sutler, who worked theater, club and after-hours gigs for $600-700 a week before he lost his mind and went to an asylum.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Then we had the Bookstore, a place called the Bookstore, after hour place. And I must mention to you, there was trumpet player named Joe Sutler that nobody mentions.
Joe Sutler. He was more famous then Louis Armstrong.

Yes, he was, and made more money. And for some reason… very sparsely now, a few people are beginning to ask me about him. His name was the biggest. He was a hard worker. He went to… he would play the theater, which was through by 11 o‟clock at night, then he would go to the nightclub and play „til two or three o‟clock in the morning, then he would go to the Bookstore, which was an after hour place to play „til… this man was making $600 and $700 a week in those days.

Well of course he blew himself out because he lost his mind and went to an asylum. I was hearing about him but I never got to play with him. I was listening to him and listening to people rave about him. Then he went to the insane asylum and he got straight and he came out and tried to play the tuba. That‟s the time I heard him but he was…
